ModMetaData.name: Venus Touch Waistlines
ModMetaData.author: Nelim
ModMetaData.description:
Decides where garments stop on the body. Works with TailorMade, which is optional, and is not affiliated with it.
TailorMade sorts apparel into classes and fits each class into a horizontal band of the body: pants into the bottom 58%, boots into the bottom 20%, chest pieces into the top 55%. Those numbers suit a body drawn with legs. On a body retexture drawn as one legless shape, 58% of the way up from the hem lands above the navel, and trousers read as a high-waisted skirt.
They are constants, and nothing exposes them. This mod makes them settings, so every leg garment of every mod is corrected at once. Nothing changes until a slider moves: the defaults are TailorMade's own values.
It also offers to lift one of TailorMade's own guards, carefully. TailorMade only bands a torso garment whose art already starts 40% of the way up the texture. That guard exists so long coats and capes keep draping to the ankles, and it is right to, but it also excludes the garments that most need shortening: a vanilla shirt is drawn over the whole body, so it stays full length and hides the trousers entirely. The option lifts the test for on-skin garments only. Shirts and tribalwear are cut where the trousers begin; dusters, parkas, jackets and robes are worn on the shell layer and still drape, and jackets are drawn as they are.
With WDI's Realistic Bodies, the shirts WDI draws for each body are not resized by TailorMade at all: they are cut on the top edge of WDI's underwear for that body, column by column, and the trousers start on the same edge, so the two always meet on the same shape. Thin, Fat and Hulk women get their own trousers, cut on their own underwear. Children have no underwear in WDI, so their line is the one their trousers start on. The option is off by default.
Vanilla trousers carry no worn graphic at all, so a mod that fills that field is still required, and this one is written for AB's Visible Pants. AB draws its trousers as a plain shell: an outline and an even fill, with no waistband, no fly and no seam. On a body drawn without legs that shell is all there is, and it reads as a shell rather than as clothing. Two options deal with it, both on by default, both applied when the game starts, and both acting only where AB is the mod supplying the texture:
[list] [*][b]General Textures Collection's trousers.[/b] General carries a retexture of the same garment, with a waistband, belt loops and a fly, but only loads it when XeoNovaDan's Visible Pants is active. With AB active instead, this mod reads those textures from General's own installed folder and uses them. Nothing is copied or redistributed: it reads what you already own, and does nothing if General is not installed. General has no child trousers. [*][b]Details on plain shells.[/b] Where there is no such retexture, a child or a body type General does not cover, it draws a waistband, a fly and seams onto AB's shell and parts the legs at the bottom. [/list]
Both are registered in this mod's own content, never in AB's or General's, and removing the mod removes them. For every body type this supplied art for, TailorMade is told to leave the trousers alone, because it would otherwise stretch art that is already drawn for the body into its band; so the pants slider does not apply to them. Turn both options off, or run without AB, and TailorMade fits the trousers and follows the slider as before. Two sliders, one for adults and one for children, move what they supply further down the body, as a fraction of its height, for a body art where they sit too high.
[b]Thanks[/b] to astryl, whose TailorMade does all the work this one merely aims, and whose MIT licence is what makes an add-on like this possible; to brrainz for Harmony; to aedbia, whose AB's Visible Pants supplies the trousers vanilla never draws; to Kas, whose General Textures Collection carries the trouser art this reads; and to the author of WDI's Realistic Bodies, whose art is the reason the problem exists at all.
[b]Made with AI.[/b] The preview and the icon were generated by an image model and recomposed by hand. The assembly, its tests and its documentation were written with Claude Code, which the commit history records as a co-author.
[b]Adoption.[/b] If I do not answer within a reasonable time after being contacted, anyone may freely update this or any other of my mods, including publishing a continuation of it. All credit must be preserved.
